title: Submission
description:
The `POST /v1/actions` response — the outcome of the engine's submit.

Externally tagged, lowercase (`{"executed": {…}}` / `{"pending": {…}}` /
`{"sealed": {…}}`).

oneOf.description: GREEN/YELLOW: executed immediately, audit sealed.
RED: queued for founder sign-off; nothing audited yet.
NEVER: sealed on the spot as rejected; never queued, never executed.

Action.description:
The action an agent submits. Reflex holds the full payload; only its
`payload_hash` crosses the wire (soma §8).

blocking.description:
Whether a caller is awaiting this outcome and cannot proceed without
it — the `blocks-active` arm of the critical bar.

Additive and defaulted, so records written before it existed parse
unchanged and it stays off the wire when false. An agent that is not
blocked does not get to claim it is.

ext.description:
Namespaced extension data (doctrine rule 13: ONE wire format —
vertical packs are interpretation libraries, never dialects).

Keys are namespaced `<vendor>.<pack>` (e.g. `soma.finance`); core
consumers ignore what they do not understand, and NOTHING load-bearing
for the gate may live here — a verb, tier, verdict, or check belongs
in the format itself or it does not exist. `soma.evidence` is RESERVED
for the evidence-provenance grades (adopted in direction 2026-08-21;
definition deferred to an operator interview — do not define it here).
See `spec/extensions.md` for the binding rules.

id.description: Opaque action id (`"act_01JX…"`, ULID-shaped in practice).

payload_hash.description: `"sha256:…"` of the full payload the plane holds off-wire.

ActionContext.description: Free-form provenance for an action (engagement / thread — soma §8).

ActionRecord.description:
Wire record 1: an agent's action submission together with reflex's
classification of it (soma §8). Carries the top-level `"reflex"` version tag.

Amount.description:
A monetary amount for `spend` classification, in minor units of a currency
(cents for USD). Compared against founder-set soft/hard caps by the
classifier.

minor_units.description: Minor units — cents for USD, pence for GBP, etc.

AttestedBy.description:
Who vouches for a sealed attestation. Until blackwall-serve signs it
(ratified precondition Q3) the only value is `executor`: the evidence is
executor-attested, never reflex-verified, and the record says so
(`spec/schemas/audit-record.schema.json` pins the `const`).

Audit.description:
The audit body. `executed_by` is always the plane — the agent never executes
(soma §8).

at.description:
When this record was sealed — RFC 3339, stamped from reflexd's clock at
seal time (EST-189).

Before this field the sealed action record carried NO instant at all
(measured on the live chain 2026-08-25: 22 `audit` records, none
timed), so nothing classified could be placed in time and every
time-windowed measurement row (Art. 72 / compliance-surfaces cat. 9)
read `not_yet`. The sign-off layer was already timed (`Signoff.at`,
`Decision.ts`, `DecisionAct.at`); this closes the gap for the
classifier's own records.

The seal instant, deliberately — not the action id's mint instant
(`act_<hex nanos>` is an id-uniqueness encoding, and mint time is not
decision time: a RED card waits on the person). `Option` like `tier`
and `policy`: absent on records sealed before the field existed, and a
reader counts those as untimed rather than guessing
(`marrow::trend::Trend` already does).

containment_attested.description:
The attestation sealed BY VALUE on the follow-up record (v3 §5, §6.3):
compact observed extracts parsed once from the relayed text, never
references to GC'd objects (D6). Requires `containment_requested` on the
same record — `dependentRequired` in the spec schema; an attestation with
no sealed request is malformed (v3 §8). Ratified 2026-09-28; nothing
sets it yet.

containment_requested.description:
The REQUESTED containment sealed on the `dispatched` record (v3 D5,
EST-318 PR b): `{profile, profile_digest, required_layers}` from the same
registry entry the card displayed — the seed id is this record's own
`policy`. The reconciler's only requested-side input; it never compares
against a fresh registry fetch. Carried onto the follow-up record.
Absent = uncontained (today). Ratified 2026-09-28; nothing sets it yet.

dispatch_ref.description:
The downstream queue's handle on dispatched work — blackwall's ULID
job id (EST-86). Present only for [`Outcome::Dispatched`]; a completed
or rejected action has nothing to reconcile against.

Without this the audit stream records that something was dispatched
and keeps no way to ask what became of it: `dispatched` is
streak-neutral, so autonomy can never be credited for work that did
in fact succeed. This is the binding that makes a reconciler possible.

dispatch_via.description:
Which queue `dispatch_ref` belongs to (EST-188). `dispatch_ref` is
executor-namespaced — blackwall's ULID job id under the blackwall
executor, the action id itself under escapement (reflex submits the
escapement task with `id = action.id`, so the two are equal by
REFLEX's construction; escapement itself does not guarantee it) — and before this field the record did not say which, so a
reader had to know the daemon's executor mode out of band to resolve
it. Present whenever `dispatch_ref` is; absent on records sealed
before the field existed (those refs are unresolvable by construction
and the dispatch reconciler skips them rather than guessing).

executed_by.description: `"reflex"` — the plane executes; the agent never does.

ext.description:
Namespaced extension data (doctrine rule 13: ONE wire format —
vertical packs are interpretation libraries, never dialects).

Keys are namespaced `<vendor>.<pack>` (e.g. `soma.finance`); core
consumers ignore what they do not understand, and NOTHING load-bearing
for the gate may live here — a verb, tier, verdict, or check belongs
in the format itself or it does not exist. `soma.evidence` is RESERVED
for the evidence-provenance grades (adopted in direction 2026-08-21;
definition deferred to an operator interview — do not define it here).
See `spec/extensions.md` for the binding rules.

halt_ref.description:
The halt receipt — which interrupt stopped this action (EST-165).
Present only for [`Outcome::Halted`]; captured AT halt time, because a
receipt looked up later may already be gone (the `run_ref` lesson).
Serialized only when present: an un-halted action must not emit
`"halt_ref": null` and imply a halt was possible but empty.

payload_hash.description:
The SAME value as the action's `payload_hash` (`"sha256:<hex>"`); binds
this record to the exact content that was gated (EST-268).

Present at every tier: before this field only a RED sign-off carried
the hash, so a GREEN/YELLOW record said what verb ran and not on what.
`Option` like its neighbours: absent on records sealed before the field
existed (readers count those as unbound rather than guessing). Never
serialized as null.

policy.description:
The policy version in force when this was decided
(`"soma/comms:send-external@v3"`) — marrow §3's citation of authority.

`Classification.policy` has existed since v0 and was never sealed, so
the chain could not answer the question the whole event-sourced design
rests on: *was this decided according to the law as it then stood?*
Folding to the record's seq reconstructs the law; this names which
grant was applied, so the two can be compared rather than assumed.

reason.description:
Why a contained action FAILED (EST-374, `spec/schemas/audit-record`
`$defs/Reason`). Absent is the norm: the SPEC schema
(`spec/schemas/audit-record`, its `allOf` invariants) allows it only on
`outcome: failed`, and only beside `containment_requested`. This type
does not enforce that; [`Audit::validate`] does, and a sealing site
calls it before appending. Never serialized as null.

run_ref.description:
blackwall's content-addressed run hash, captured when the reconciler
observes a terminal `done` (EST-86).

Captured at reconcile time rather than looked up on demand because the
job record's retention is a *pod lifetime*, not a duration — after a
replacement the `dispatch_ref` no longer resolves to anything, and this
is the only durable pointer left to the custody record.

tier.description:
The tier this action was classified at (marrow §6).

Absent on records sealed before this field existed. `Option` rather
than a default so the calibration read can count those separately
instead of silently attributing them to a tier nobody chose — an
unattributable record is a fact about the chain, not a GREEN one.

AuditRecord.description:
Wire record 3: the sealed, append-only audit record that feeds the trust
ledger (soma §8). Written by an [`crate::audit::AuditSink`].

basis.description:
Why this tier — the earned-autonomy basis
(`"verb not yet earned (ledger: 11/25 clean)"`, soma §8).

ext.description:
Namespaced extension data (doctrine rule 13: ONE wire format —
vertical packs are interpretation libraries, never dialects).

Keys are namespaced `<vendor>.<pack>` (e.g. `soma.finance`); core
consumers ignore what they do not understand, and NOTHING load-bearing
for the gate may live here — a verb, tier, verdict, or check belongs
in the format itself or it does not exist. `soma.evidence` is RESERVED
for the evidence-provenance grades (adopted in direction 2026-08-21;
definition deferred to an operator interview — do not define it here).
See `spec/extensions.md` for the binding rules.

never_provenance.description:
Present exactly when `tier` is [`Tier::Never`] — see
[`NeverProvenance`]. Absent on non-NEVER classifications and on
records sealed before this field existed; absent reads UNKNOWN, never
a defaulted class nobody asserted.

policy.description: The policy id that classified this action (`"soma/comms:send-external@v3"`).

ContainmentAttested.description:
The audit-seal of an [`AppliedContainment`] (v3 §5, §6.3), sealed BY VALUE
on the follow-up audit record as `containment_attested`. Requires
`containment_requested` on the same record — `dependentRequired` in the
spec schema; an attestation with no sealed request is malformed (v3 §8).

The reconciler, not this type, checks `profile_digest` equality against the
requested side and that `enforced_by` covers every sealed `required_layer`;
the schema pins shape, not value equality.

signature_verified.description:
reflex verified serve's signature over this attestation before
sealing it (CER-2276 §8). Required: under Q3 there is no unsigned path
to seal. `attested_by` stays `executor`, because serve is still the one
that observed the layers.

ContainmentRequested.description:
The audit-seal projection of a [`Containment`] (v3 D5; EST-318 PR b): what
the `dispatched` audit record carries as `containment_requested`, and the
ONLY requested-side input the reconciler compares an attestation against —
never a fresh registry fetch.

No `policy`, and the audit record's own `policy` is NOT it: `Audit.policy`
is the classification policy, while `Containment::policy` is the seed row's
(they differ in vector valid/07). So the request cannot be re-hashed from
this record; [`Self::containment_sha256`] seals the hash instead
(CER-2276 §7 step 6). Shape pinned by
`spec/schemas/audit-record.schema.json` `$defs.ContainmentRequested`
(soma#408), which is `additionalProperties: false`.

containment_sha256.description:
[`Containment::sha256`] of the request, sealed at dispatch. The
attestation's `payload.containment_sha256` must equal it EXACTLY
(CER-2276 §7 step 6); it is never recomputed from this record, which
lacks `policy`.

isolation_tier.description:
The ISOLATION tier (`kata-clh`, `runc`), copied from the registry
profile's own `tier` (soma#426). Not the governance tier. Sealed, never
compared: the attestation carries no tier. Absent on a request built
without the profile text.

placement_deadline_secs.description:
How long the run may wait for placement at its tier before it fails
`containment-unschedulable` (soma#426). Sealed with `isolation_tier`:
the SPEC schema's `dependentRequired` requires both or neither; this
type alone does not enforce it; [`ContainmentRequested::validate`]
does, and `From<&ContainedDispatch>` always sets both. Non-zero by type.

DispatchVia.description:
The queue a dispatched action was admitted to — the namespace of
[`Audit::dispatch_ref`] (EST-188; `spec/transport.md` §6).

Lowercase on the wire (`"blackwall"` / `"escapement"`). A closed enum on
purpose: a new queue is a new edge in CANON §1c and a new poll in the
dispatch reconciler, not a string somebody typed.

oneOf.description:
reflexd → blackwall-serve direct: `dispatch_ref` is blackwall's ULID
job id, resolved at `GET {BLACKWALL_SERVE}/v1/jobs/{ref}`.

reflexd → escapement (governed dispatch, 2026-08-25): `dispatch_ref`
is the action id, resolved at `GET {ESCAPEMENT_SERVE}/jobs/{ref}`.

LedgerDelta.description:
The per-(agent, verb) delta this outcome applies to the trust ledger
(soma §8). `clean` is the running clean-streak count after this execution.

NeverProvenance.description:
Reflex's verdict on an action: the tier, the policy that decided it, and the
human-readable basis (soma §8). Produced by [`crate::classifier::classify`].
WHY a NEVER seal exists — the provenance class of the sealed rule
(EST-169; AI Act Art. 5 posture; drift-ledger row 6).

`Tier::Never` was one undifferentiated value, which flattens three very
different claims into one glyph: "a statute forbids this", "our policy
forbids this", and "we do not do this". An auditor needs to know which —
a law-sealed action cannot be unsealed by any operator ruling, a
policy-sealed one can be re-ruled, a convention-sealed one documents a
norm. The classifier stamps this at seal time; it is never inferred
after the fact.

oneOf.description: A statutory or regulatory obligation seals it. No operator path.

An organization-adopted rule seals it (spend hard caps, the sign
ratchet floor, reflex's own protected-target invariants). Re-ruling
is an operator act on the policy, never on the record.
A norm or practice seals it — documented, not legislated.

Outcome.description:
Terminal outcome of an action (soma §8).

`Dispatched` is deliberately distinct from `Executed` (EST-79): a
queue-accepting executor (blackwall dispatch) has only *enqueued* the
work — the effect does not yet exist in the world, so the audit stream
must not claim it does. The trust ledger's replay treats `dispatched` as
streak-neutral (neither an increment nor a reset), matching the live
engine: autonomy is never credited for unproven work.

oneOf.description:
The dispatched work's fate is genuinely unknown (EST-86).

Emitted by the reconciler when blackwall answers 404 for a job it
previously accepted: the record died with the pod, and blackwall's
retention section is explicit that `pending`, `running`, `done` **and**
`failed` are all lost together. A 404 therefore cannot distinguish
"never ran" from "ran to completion and the receipt was destroyed".

It is deliberately neither `Failed` nor `Executed`. Recording a failure
would teach the ledger something false; recording success would credit
autonomy for unproven work. Like [`Outcome::Dispatched`] it is
streak-neutral, and re-dispatch requires operator sign-off — a gate
plane must never duplicate an effect that may already exist.

A human pulled the cord (EST-165; AI Act Art. 14(4)(e) — the
halt/interrupt duty). The action was stopped by an operator
intervention, not by the gate's own classification and not by a
downstream failure.

Terminal and STREAK-NEUTRAL: a halt is a fact about a human
exercising oversight, not evidence the agent erred (that would make
every use of the halt duty count against autonomy and teach operators
not to pull it) and not an approval either. `Audit::halt_ref` carries
the halt receipt, captured at halt time — the `run_ref` durability
lesson: pointers resolved later resolve to nothing.

Reason.description:
The closed set of failure causes an audit record may name (EST-374;
`spec/schemas/audit-record.schema.json` `$defs/Reason`). Every value is
containment-scoped. The tier is never downgraded, so no reason describes a
downgrade.

oneOf.description:
The attestation is missing, unverifiable, does not cover every sealed
`required_layer`, or names a different `profile_digest` (v3 §6.2).
Still queued at `placement_deadline_secs`, so nothing ran (v3 §6.4).
serve refused: the profile changed since the card was signed (v3 §4).
serve refused: the attestation exceeds the result bound (v3 §3).

RecipientClass.description:
A recipient classification a policy can gate `send-external` on
(`spend(<$500, known-vendor)`, soma §5.1; `"known-counterparty"`, §8).

The taxonomy is closed on purpose: an unrecognized recipient class fails to
deserialize rather than silently classifying as benign.

oneOf.description: Inside the org — internal writes, colleagues.
A vendor already on the books.
A counterparty in an existing engagement (soma §8 example).
No prior relationship — the most conservative outbound class.
The public / an unbounded audience (publish-adjacent).

SealedLayer.description:
One layer's evidence as SEALED on the audit record — the transport form
([`EnforcedLayer`], evidence as JSON text) parsed once into a value.

The seam, agreed with the reflex lane 2026-09-28: the transport carries the
attestation as text (`JobStatus`/`TaskResult` are `Eq`, and #412's bytes
are custody-proven); the RECORD seals the parsed value, as the spec allows
(`EnforcedLayer.evidence` has no `type`). reflex parses exactly once, at
the reconciler, through [`ContainmentAttested::executor`].

evidence.description: The compact OBSERVED extract, by value.

SignatureVerified.description:
Proof, sealed on the audit record, that reflex verified the attestation's
signature before sealing it (§8). Required on
[`crate::containment::ContainmentAttested`]: under Q3 there is no unsigned
path to seal a contained `Executed`.

iat.description: The signed `iat` the chain was validated as of.

leaf_serial.description:
The leaf certificate's serial: the DER INTEGER content octets with
leading 0x00 octets stripped (at least one kept), lowercase hex, two
characters per octet (§8). Matches `openssl x509 -serial` compared
case-insensitively. webpki's `Cert::serial()` includes the sign byte:
strip it before sealing.

Tier.description:
The four-rung gate ladder (soma §5.1), generalized from godseat's cluster
Green/Yellow/Red/Never to enterprise verbs.

Serializes UPPERCASE to match the §8 wire (`"tier": "RED"`).

oneOf.description: Autonomous; audited. (read, triage, draft, internal file/ticket, report)
Notify-and-proceed; the founder can veto within a window.
Blocks on named-human sign-off.
Sealed; **no sign-off path exists** (soma §5.1).

Verb.description:
The starter verb taxonomy for instance #0 (soma §5.1).

Serializes kebab-case to match the wire (`file-internal`, `send-external`,
`hire-engage`, `grant-access`, `delete-destroy`, `commit-code`).

oneOf.description: Delegated to terrarium's existing commit gates (soma §5.1).

VerbParams.description:
Parameters a verb carries that policies gate on (soma §5.1: "amount,
recipient class, visibility"). Every field is optional — a `read` carries
none, a `spend` carries an `amount`, a `send-external` a `recipient_class`.

`None` fields are omitted from the wire (`skip_serializing_if`) so the
serialized `params` object stays as tight as the §8 examples.

target.description:
The resource acted on, as the submitter declares it. reflexd seals an
action whose target names its own policy or state as NEVER
(`reflex::classifier::ProtectedTargets`, EST-459). Self-declared, so
that rule is a second line: it stops an honest or mistaken agent, and
the structural barriers are elsewhere (EST-460).

visibility.description: For `publish` — how widely it is exposed.

VerifiedBy.description:
Who verified an attestation's signature. A single value today; a type
rather than a string so a record cannot claim any other verifier.

Visibility.description: Payload visibility a policy can gate `publish` on (soma §5.1).
